hook: *8* Dominican Spots Uptown Still Gets Right
dek: Eight uptown Dominican spots, checked this week, with addresses, hours and what to order.

slides.label: Little DR
slides.text: Washington Heights and Inwood is *Little DR*, where the rotisserie chicken spins in every window.

slides.label: Malecon
slides.text: *Malecon* has served rotisserie chicken since 1987, 4141 Broadway, open till midnight weekends.

slides.label: Floridita
slides.text: *Floridita* fuses Cuban and Dominican since 1995 and never closes: *24 hours*, 4162 Broadway.

slides.label: Elsa
slides.text: At *Elsa La Reina del Chicharrón*, you order pork by the weight and build your plate from the counter.

slides.label: La Casa
slides.text: *La Casa del Mofongo* brings cocktails, live music and a mofongo menu, open till 4 a.m. weekends.

slides.label: Mamajuana Cafe
slides.text: *Mamajuana Cafe* is where you take someone you want to impress, orchids, wine list, chef Ricardo Cardona.

slides.label: First Order
slides.text: First time? Start with *mangú con los tres golpes*, the breakfast of champions uptown.

slides.label: The Takeaway
slides.text: Pick one spot this week, bring someone who's never had mangú, and *let the neighborhood do the rest*.

caption_linkedin:
Eight Dominican restaurants in Washington Heights and Inwood prove something simple: hospitality built on consistency outlasts hype.

Malecon has run since 1987. Floridita stays open 24 hours, every day, since 1995. Mamajuana Cafe grew from one Dyckman Street room into locations across the Bronx, New Jersey and Connecticut, built around chef Ricardo Cardona's take on Nuevo Latino cuisine. None of that happens by accident, it happens because operators show up, keep hours real, and let word of mouth do the marketing.

For founders building anything uptown, downtown or outside New York, the lesson is the same: the businesses that last are the ones that never stopped being exactly what the neighborhood needed.

What's the one business in your neighborhood that's been consistent for decades?
